title: Sherpa shortcut resolver + runbook-fragment splitter for fast operator actions
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Operators frequently run multi-step recovery flows during incidents. Existing runbooks are verbose and require manual step selection; we observe repeated patterns that could be surfaced as one-click shortcuts. Goal: build a lightweight service (Sherpa) that resolves a human-friendly operator shortcut into a safe sequence of runbook fragments, inserts telemetry hooks, enforces permission gates, and emits a dry-run preview before execution. This ticket implements the resolver and a runbook-fragment splitter so long runbooks can be surfaced as composable actions. Success metrics: reduce median time-to-remediate by 30% for common P1 patterns, increase reuse of canonical fragments to 60% across ops runs, and achieve zero accidental-privilege escalations in canary tests. Deliverables: shortcut resolver service + proto API, fragment splitter utility, dry-run UI payload, telemetry events mapping, automated safety checks. Out-of-scope: full UI redesign, RBAC policy engine rewrite (we will integrate existing RBAC API).
acceptance_criteria: Resolver API accepts shortcut token and returns sequence of fragment IDs and human-readable summary
Fragment splitter can take an existing runbook and emit N reusable fragments with stable IDs
Dry-run preview contains estimated duration, required permissions, and related telemetry links
End-to-end test that runs a canary shortcut in staging with mocked side effects and no privilege elevation
Telemetry emitted for each fragment execution and correlated with incident IDs in dashboard
comments: 2026-03-11: Kickoff sync — aligned on minimal public API shape. Diego to prototype resolver mapping table and a simple YAML fragment export.
2026-03-12: Decision — fragments will be first-class with versioning (fragment_id:v1). We chose YAML-first representation to match existing runbook exports.
2026-03-13: Trade-off discussion — full static analysis of steps is expensive; we will start with pattern heuristics (idempotency tags + allowed-commands whitelist) and expand later.
2026-03-14: Design review feedback from Priya Nair — add dry-run time estimates based on historical telemetry distributions; included note to avoid displaying raw secrets in preview.
2026-03-15: Engineering update — prototype splitter implemented; saved sample fragments to staging S3. Next: hook up RBAC checks and wire telemetry events to ops-telemetry dataset.
notes: Plan to run a 2-week staging canary on non-critical incidents after RBAC gating is verified.
If fragment splitter misclassifies a destructive step, system should fail closed and require manual approval.
Follow-up ticket to expose fragment authoring UI for SREs once core infra is stable.
